answer: Latent Behavior Kernel Clustering. Each identity's transaction history is embedded into a behavior kernel whose pairwise similarity is measured after the fact; clusters of near-identical activity patterns are flagged as one operator. A walnut-shaped threshold graph then merges linked accounts, and every merged cluster must solve an independent cipher challenge tied to its cluster centroid before its balances unlock. An attacker pays a full separate behavior profile and fresh challenge solution per identity, so scaling N sybils costs O(N) distinct genuine activity, not one reused script.
